title: Unit Test: Chemical Reactions and Equations
subject: Science
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Internal choice is given in some questions.
Section A: 1 mark each. Section B: 2 marks each. Section C: 3 marks each. Section D: 5 marks. Section E: case-based, 4 marks.
Write balanced chemical equations wherever asked. Mention physical states where possible.

questions.q: Which of the following is a correctly balanced chemical equation?
questions.answer: (b) 3Fe + 4H_{2}O → Fe_{3}O_{4} + 4H_{2}. Both sides have 3 Fe, 8 H and 4 O.

questions.q: When dilute hydrochloric acid is added to zinc granules, the gas evolved is:
2AgCl(s) → 2Ag(s) + Cl_{2}(g) takes place in sunlight. This is an example of:
In the reaction CuO + H_{2} → Cu + H_{2}O, the substance that gets oxidised is:
questions.answer: (b) H_{2}. It gains oxygen to form H_{2}O.

questions.q: Which of the following is an exothermic process?
questions.answer: (b) Respiration. Glucose is oxidised and energy is released.

questions.q: **Assertion (A):** The blue colour of copper sulphate solution fades when an iron nail is dipped in it.  **Reason (R):** Iron is more reactive than copper and displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.
questions.answer: (a). Fe + CuSO_{4} → FeSO_{4} + Cu. The solution turns from blue to light green.

questions.q: Why should a magnesium ribbon be cleaned with sandpaper before burning it in air? Write the balanced equation for its burning.
questions.answer: The ribbon has a layer of magnesium oxide (formed by reaction with air) on its surface, which stops it from burning easily. Sandpaper removes this layer. 2Mg(s) + O_{2}(g) → 2MgO(s)

questions.q: What is a precipitation reaction? Give one example with a balanced chemical equation.
questions.answer: A reaction in which an insoluble solid (precipitate) is formed. Na_{2}SO_{4}(aq) + BaCl_{2}(aq) → BaSO_{4}(s) + 2NaCl(aq), which gives a white precipitate of BaSO_{4}.

or.q: Why are bags of chips flushed with nitrogen gas? Name the process this prevents.
or.answer: Nitrogen is unreactive and replaces oxygen in the packet, so the fats and oils in the chips are not oxidised. This prevents rancidity (change in smell and taste).

questions.q: A solution of a substance 'X' is used for whitewashing walls.

subparts.q: Name 'X' and write its chemical formula.
Write the balanced equation for the reaction of X with water.
Why does the wall get a shiny finish two to three days after whitewashing?
subparts.answer: Ca(OH)_{2} reacts slowly with CO_{2} in air to form a thin, shiny layer of calcium carbonate: Ca(OH)_{2} + CO_{2} → CaCO_{3} + H_{2}O

questions.q: State the type of each of the following reactions:

A reaction in which one substance is oxidised and another is reduced at the same time.

subparts.q: In the reaction ZnO + C → Zn + CO, identify the substance oxidised and the substance reduced. Give reasons.
subparts.answer: C is oxidised (it gains oxygen to form CO). ZnO is reduced (it loses oxygen to form Zn).

subparts.q: What is corrosion? Give two ways to prevent the rusting of iron.
subparts.answer: Corrosion is the slow eating away of a metal when it is attacked by substances around it such as moisture, oxygen and acids (e.g. rusting of iron). Prevention (any two): painting, oiling/greasing, galvanising, chrome plating, making alloys.

or.q: (a) What do you observe when ferrous sulphate crystals are heated in a boiling tube? Write the balanced equation and name the type of reaction. [3]   (b) Why is respiration considered an exothermic reaction? Write the equation. [2]
or.answer: (a) The green crystals first lose water and then turn reddish-brown, and a smell of burning sulphur is noticed. 2FeSO_{4}(s) → Fe_{2}O_{3}(s) + SO_{2}(g) + SO_{3}(g), on heating. This is thermal decomposition. (b) In respiration glucose combines with oxygen in our cells and energy is released: C_{6}H_{12}O_{6}(aq) + 6O_{2}(g) → 6CO_{2}(g) + 6H_{2}O(l) + energy.

sections.title: Section E
sections.note: Read the passage and answer the questions that follow.

questions.q: In a class activity, students heated lead nitrate powder in a boiling tube. Brown fumes were given off and a yellowish residue was left behind. In another observation, a copper vessel kept in the open for a few months developed a green coating on its surface.

subparts.q: Name the brown gas given off when lead nitrate is heated.
What type of reaction is the heating of lead nitrate?
What is the green coating on the copper vessel, and why does it form?
subparts.answer: Basic copper carbonate. Copper reacts slowly with moist carbon dioxide (and oxygen) in the air. This is corrosion of copper.
